lessons_control.note: pre_lessons is each hunter's own sum before it read researcher_us/LESSONS.md. edge_resolve.py ranks it against the same realised move as the key, which is the only thing that can tell the guidance file apart from a habit.

language_control.note: RETIRED 2026-09-22: the European and Canadian hunters now run one bilingual pass and emit no freeze, so this is 0/0 on every run sealed after that date. On earlier runs pre_local is each hunter's own sum after the ENGLISH pass and before the local pass; eu_resolve.py ranks it against the same realised move as the key, per market, and does not pool the UK (where the second pass varied source locality) with Germany and France (where it varied language).

note: Ranked on impact_sum: the hunters' signed per-finding sizes, added up, in points of spot. No call and no threshold -- cut wherever you like afterwards, which is what keeps the ranking question answerable at every k. `conviction` (abs of the key) is where the direction skill lives: over all events the sign is a coin flip, above the median conviction it is 74%. conviction_floor is a floor on emphasis in the note, never a filter on this file. Everything under `diagnostics` was measured as neutral or subtractive and decides nothing -- see researcher_us/EDGE_ANALYSIS.md.

findings.finding: The Feb-2027 DPU forecast of ¥2,450 was set in April without Toyosu Prime Square: ¥29.4bn, appraisal NOI yield 3.7%, 3.3% after depreciation, acquired 2026-09-30 inside the Feb-2027 period and debt-funded. That forecast also leaned on an ¥805m reserve drawdown (about ¥146 a unit), and the asset manager's stated goal is DPU growth of 3% a year plus α. So this print, which must also issue a first Aug-2027 forecast, is more likely to raise the forward DPU path (toward roughly ¥2,480-2,520) than to hold it.

Raises have been bought weakly or sold.

findings.finding: Aug-2026 (49th period) DPU will likely print slightly above the ¥2,450 forecast. Each of the last two periods came in at or above the forecast set six months earlier (Feb-26: 2,414 actual vs 2,380), and the Hamamatsu Act Tower first-tranche gain (sale ¥17.15bn in total vs ¥14.7bn appraisal) is already inside this period's plan.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: A reported-period beat of about 1.4% (Feb-26) came with -1.69% on 2026-04-22. The reported period has not moved this name on its own.

findings.finding: Q3 (Jul-Sep) laps an easy base: same-store sales were 103.8% in Q3 2025 (Jul 102.2, Aug 107.1, Sep 101.6) against 108.5% in Q2 2025. Average spend is still carried by the November 2025 price rise, and the H1 2026 operating margin was 11.7%. Q2 operating profit grew +29.8% while the H2 plan needs only +19.7%, so Q3 OP is likely ~1,040-1,060m against a plan-implied ~1,000m, and 9-month progress lands around 75% against 70.2% at the same point in 2025.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q1 2026 OP +93.5% beat, released 2026-04-21 15:30: +0.12% next session, then -3.80%. Q2 2026 beat plus upgrade, 2026-07-22: +2.29% (FISCO: 'upside was expected, reaction limited'). Q3 2025 9-month OP 10.9% below the internal plan, 2025-10-21: -1.95%. Close-to-close from Yahoo daily bars.

findings.finding: A forecast revision at Q3 is unlikely: kabutan's revision record shows the company revised only at Q2 in 2023, 2024 and 2026, never at Q3. The stock trades at 2,950, above Tokai Tokyo's raised 2,800 target (2026-08-13) and about 23% above its 2,398 pre-Q2 close. So a beat with the plan held risks a sell-the-news (出尽くし) reaction, as Q1 2026 showed.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q1 2026, plan held with a strong beat: +0.12% then -3.80% (FISCO 2026-04-22: 'short-term sense of news being out'). FY2025 print with a flat-ish new guide (OP +1%): -3.16% on 2026-01-21.

lessons_applied: Rule 1 / open question 4: the negative rests on public information (the revision record, the run-up) and a run-in short read was wrong once already, so finding 2 goes from -0.8 to -0.5 and p_up from 48 to 49.
Rule 2: I wrote the strongest positive into baseline_tension and had already looked for it (finding 1, no Q3 dividend or buyback history); no further change.

findings.finding: IFIS consensus implies Oct-Dec ordinary profit of about 69.0bn: 9M 181.3bn less H1 112.4bn. That is about 13% above the ~61bn Q2 the Nikkei 観測 implies (H1 OP ~110bn less Q1 49.0bn). DISCO's July guide for Jul-Sep (OP 55.9bn) came in below a consensus of 60bn+ and the stock fell about 12%, so another conservative guide below this bar is the likeliest shape of the release.
findings.source_date: 2026-10-22 (fetched; consensus date not shown on the page)
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: When the one-quarter-ahead guide undershot consensus at the July 2026 print (Jul-Sep OP 55.9bn vs 60bn+), the stock fell about 12% the next session (kabutan/Fisco 2026-07-24; baseline -12.27). When the FY guide came in near consensus at the Jan 2026 print, the stock rose about 17% (kabutan 2026-01-22). The Apr 2026 Q1 guide of +22% YoY drew a flat-to-negative reaction (-3.78). In the baseline, the last two October prints rose: +7.67 in 2024 and +5.03 in 2025.

findings.finding: The Jul-Sep quarter is already out. On 10-06 the non-consolidated flash put H1 sales at 213.6bn against a 201.1bn plan (+6.2%) and Q2 shipments at a record 123.9bn (+60% YoY, +6.4% QoQ); the stock fell 6.3% on 10-07. On 10-19 a Nikkei report put H1 OP near 110bn, about 8bn over the 104.9bn plan, and Fisco called it in line. That leaves the consolidated H1 about 2% under IFIS's 112.4bn ordinary-profit consensus.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Pre-released quarters have been sold or ignored: -6.3% on the 10-07 flash, a 'sharp fall' on the 07-07 Q1 flash, 'limited reaction' to the Jan 9 flash, and 'no surprise' on the 07-21 and 10-19 観測 reports (kabutan).

findings.finding: On 10-15 TSMC, the largest buyer of DISCO's advanced-packaging grinders and dicers, beat its Q3 guide (US$46.7bn) and guided Q4 to $52.3-54.3bn. It held FY2026 capex at $60-64bn after Q3 capex of about $13.8bn, which arithmetically implies a large Q4 step-up. With DISCO's record Q2 shipments and its shipped-but-not-yet-accepted inventory build (Q1 inventory +11.6bn), this argues for a firm Oct-Dec shipment and sales plan.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: There is no clean history of DISCO reacting to a customer's capex. On the 2026-10-15 session the Japanese semicap names fell sharply (DISCO -8.5%), so the market did not read the run-up to TSMC's print as positive for DISCO.

findings.finding: The interim dividend forecast is 171 yen (+42), set against an H1 net profit plan of 73.8bn. With H1 profit running about 5% over plan on the 観測, the interim dividend will likely be raised modestly with the results, as it was at the October 2025 interim print.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: At FY prints DISCO's dividend increases (+68 yen on the FY2025 year-end, Apr 2026) did not lift the stock (-3.78). Dividend changes are mechanical with profit, and the stock does not react to them separately.

outside_window.finding: SK hynix (HBM, a major DISCO grinder customer) reports Q3 2026 on 2026-10-27/28. The Hana estimate is OP +29% QoQ. This is after the window.

lessons_applied: Rule 1 (a negative resting on a series the market already has): the pre-released quarter finding moved from -0.2 to 0.0, because the flash and the 観測 are public and were sold.

Rule 2 (check the sign): the strongest positive (a firm guide on TSMC's Q4 capex, a dividend nudge) was already looked for and filed. p_up moved 48 to 49, so expected_move_pct went from -0.30 to -0.15.
The guidance finding (-1.0) stayed: it rests on what the release ADDS, not on a visible miss.
